questions.stemHtml: The histopathological findings from a duodenal biopsy from a 38-year-old female with a 2 months history of diarrhea, bloating, and unintentional weight loss are shown below. Intraepithelial lymphocytes ( CD8+) express which cell maker in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
NKG2D
  • The given clinical history of diarrhea and weight loss and a histopathological image showing villus atrophy and crypt hyperplasia is suggestive of Celiac disease.
  • It is caused by the immune system's reaction to gluten, which damages the lining of the small intestine. Intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs), a type of CD8+ T cell in the small intestine, are involved in this process.
  • IELs express a cell surface receptor called NKG2D, which binds to stress-induced ligands on epithelial cells, contributing to the damage


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 612,613

questions.stem: All of the following are histological features of celiac disease except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Increase in mucosal thickness

Celiac disease may be associated with mucosal inflammation but there is no increased mucosal thickness, rather there is a loss of mucosal and brush-border surface area which probably accounts for the malabsorption.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 612,613

questions.stem: Which of the following antibodies is not associated with celiac disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Antinuclear antibody

ANA is a type of autoantibody that is found in individuals with autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but it is not typically associated with celiac disease.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 612,613

questions.stem: Which is the cause of malabsorption in Whipple's disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Impaired lymphatic transport
  • Malabsorption in Whipple's disease is caused by impaired lymphatic transport due to the infiltration of the intestinal wall by foamy macrophages containing the bacterium Tropheryma whipplei.
  • This results in the obstruction of the lymphatic vessels, leading to impaired fat absorption and subsequent malabsorption syndrome.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 619,620

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old patient presented with diarrhea, weight loss, and arthralgia. An intestinal biopsy was performed and a diagram of which is given below. Based on the histological features what is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Whipple disease

The given clinical scenario with a history of diarrhea, weight loss, and arthralgia and a histopathological image showing foamy macrophages suggests the diagnosis



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 612,613

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding hyperplastic polyps is false?

options.label: A
options.text: More commonly found in the left colon

options.label: C
options.text: Histologically composed of mature goblet and absorptive cells

options.label: D
options.text: These polyps have high malignant potential

questions.answerText: These polyps have high malignant potential
questions.solutionHtml:
These polyps have high malignant potential

Hyperplastic polyps are benign colorectal polyps with a very low risk of malignant potential.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 627,628

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not true regarding Juvenile Polyposis?

options.label: A
options.text: Rectum is the most common site of polyp

options.label: C
options.text: Cystically dilated glands with mucus seen histologically

questions.solutionHtml:
Common after 10 years of age

The polyps in Juvenile Polyposis develop in children or young adults, usually in children <5 years of age.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 627,628

questions.stem: A 28-year-old female presents with a history of recurrent abdominal pain, vomiting, and dark-colored stools. She has a history of multiple polyps in the small intestine and pigmented lesions on her lips and oral mucosa. Which of the following syndromes is most likely responsible for her symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
  • The given clinical history is suggestive of Peutz-jeers syndrome.
  • PJS is characterized by the presence of hamartomatous polyps in the gastrointestinal tract, which can cause abdominal pain, obstruction, and bleeding.
  • Additionally, the patient's history of pigmented macules on her buccal mucosa and lower lip is consistent with the mucocutaneous pigmentation commonly seen in PJS


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 626,627

questions.stem: All of the mentioned syndromes have autosomal dominant patterns of inheritance except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cronkhite Canada syndrome

Cronkhite Canada syndrome is a rare, non-inherited disorder that is characterized by the development of multiple gastrointestinal polyps along with other symptoms such as hair loss, nail abnormalities, and skin pigmentation changes.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 627

questions.stemHtml: A 3-year-old child presented with a pedunculated rectal polyp. Polypectomy was done and sent for histopathological examination, a picture of which is given below, classify the type of polyp:
questions.solutionHtml:
Juvenile rectal polyp
  • The given clinical history and a histopathological image showing dilated glands filled with mucin is suggestive of a Juvenile rectal polyp.
  • Juvenile polyps are the most common type of colorectal polyps in children, and they are usually pedunculated with a smooth surface.
  • Usually <3cm in diameter
  • Histologically, they are characterized by cystically dilated glands lined by normal-appearing epithelium.
  • These polyps are benign and usually do not require any further intervention after polypectomy.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 626,627

questions.stemHtml: By analyzing the histological features of adenoma classify it into its subclass:
questions.solutionHtml:
Villous adenoma
  • The given histopathological image of the polyp showing finger-like projection is of a Villous adenoma.
  • Villous adenoma have highest malignant potential


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 603,604

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Familial adenomatous polyposis?

options.label: A
options.text: Multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon

options.label: B
options.text: Single large adenomatous polyp in the colon

questions.answerText: Multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon

Multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon is a characteristic feature of Familial adenomatous polyposis.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 603,604

questions.stem: A 35-year-old female presents with a history of endometrial cancer, and on further questioning, you learn that her father was diagnosed with colon cancer at the age of 60. Based on this information, which of the following conditions should you consider as a potential diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lynch syndrome
  • The given clinical history of endometrial cancer, in addition to a family history of colon cancer, suggests the diagnosis of Hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC), also known as Lynch syndrome.


  • It was originally described based on familial clustering of cancers at several sites including the colorectum, endometrium, stomach, ovary, ureters, brain, small bowel, hepatobiliary tract, pancreas, and skin.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 630

questions.stem: Which of the following genes is commonly mutated in patients with HNPCC (Hereditary Non-Polyposis Colorectal Cancer)?
questions.solutionHtml:
MSH2
  • HNPCC is a hereditary condition that predisposes individuals to colorectal cancer and other malignancies.
  • It is caused by inherited mutations in genes involved in DNA repair.
  • The most common genes mutated in HNPCC are MSH2 and MLH1, which are involved in DNA mismatch repair.
  • Colon cancers in HNPCC patients tend to occur at younger ages than sporadic colon cancers and are often located in the right colon.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 227

questions.stemHtml: Colonic biopsy from a patient presented with bleeding per rectum and change in bowel habits from 1-2 years. HPE picture shown below, what is your diagnosis based on the histological findings?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenocarcinoma

The given clinical history of bleeding per rectum with HPE showing tall columnar cells that resemble dysplastic epithelium is indicative of glandular tissue undergoing malignant transformation. Hence, the diagnosis is Adenocarcinoma.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 630

questions.stem: Which gene is first mutated in adenoma to adenocarcinoma sequence?
questions.solutionHtml:
APC
  • The adenoma to adenocarcinoma sequence is a process of tumorigenesis in which a normal glandular tissue progresses to adenoma, and then to adenocarcinoma through a series of genetic mutations.
  • The first mutation in this sequence is a loss of function mutation in the APC (Adenomatous polyposis coli) gene, which leads to the formation of adenomas.
  • Subsequent mutations in other genes, such as KRAS, TP53, and MLH1, lead to the progression of adenomas to adenocarcinomas.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 630,631
